name: Wayfair Competitor Monitoring Agent Ud Final

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-Q4_K_M.gguf", messages: [ { role: "system", content: `You are a senior competitive analyst writing an Executive Summary for Wayfair's strategy team. TASK: Write a compelling Executive Summary comparing Wayfair vs Amazon and Walmart in this rug category. REQUIREMENTS: 1. Lead with the single most important competitive insight 2. Include 5-6 key bullet points covering: - Price positioning (Wayfair vs Amazon vs Walmart) - Product assortment differences across all three - Rating/review comparison - Key competitive advantage for Wayfair - Walmart-specific opportunities or threats - Main strategic opportunity 3. Add a "Strategic Implications" paragraph (2-3 sentences) OUTPUT FORMAT (HTML only, no markdown):

Executive Summary

Key Competitive Insight

[Single most important finding about Wayfair vs Amazon vs Walmart]

Key Findings

  • [Topic]: [Insight]

Strategic Implications

[What this means for Wayfair's strategy]

` }, { role: "user", content: `CATEGORY: ${$('Input Parser').first().json.categoryDisplayName} WAYFAIR PRODUCTS: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Wayfair Response').first().json.wayfair_products?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)} AMAZON COMPETITOR DATA: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Amazon Response').first().json.amazonProducts?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)} WALMART COMPETITOR DATA: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Walmart Response').first().json.walmartProducts?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)}` } ], stream: false }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-Q4_K_M.gguf", messages: [ { role: "system", content: `You are a pricing strategist. Analyze pricing across Wayfair, Amazon, and Walmart. TASK: Create Pricing Insights & Whitespace Analysis with visual elements. ANALYZE: 1. Price band distribution per competitor (budget <$100, mid $100-300, premium $300+) 2. Count products in each band for each retailer 3. Price gaps and underserved segments 4. Whitespace opportunities (prioritized as High/Medium/Low) OUTPUT FORMAT (HTML only, no markdown):

Pricing Insights

Price Distribution by Retailer

Budget (<$100) W: [X] | A: [Y] | Wm: [Z]
Mid ($100-$300) W: [X] | A: [Y] | Wm: [Z]
Premium ($300+) W: [X] | A: [Y] | Wm: [Z]

Analysis: [2-3 sentences about price distribution patterns]

Whitespace Analysis

Market Gaps & Opportunities

🎯 [High Priority Opportunity Title]

[Description of the gap - what price range, what's missing, why it matters]

High Priority

Why? [Brief justification]

🎯 [Another High Priority Opportunity]

[Description]

High Priority

Why? [Brief justification]

⚡ [Medium Priority Opportunity]

[Description]

Medium Priority

📊 [Low Priority Opportunity]

[Description]

Low Priority
IMPORTANT: - Use actual product counts from the data for each price band - Include 2-3 high priority, 1-2 medium priority, and 1 low priority opportunities - Do NOT output a price gap heatmap; it is generated separately from the data - Make opportunities consistent with the PRECOMPUTED counts in the user message (do not invent counts) - Use emojis as shown (🎯, ⚡, 📊, 🔥, ⚠️, 🟢) - W = Wayfair, A = Amazon, Wm = Walmart in the band chart` }, { role: "user", content: `CATEGORY: ${$('Input Parser').first().json.categoryDisplayName} PRECOMPUTED PRICE BAND COUNTS (products with a price; use EXACTLY these numbers in the band chart and analysis): ${(() => { const band = items => { const r = { b: 0, m: 0, p: 0 }; (items || []).forEach(i => { const x = parseFloat(String(i.price ?? '').replace(/,/g, '')); if (!Number.isFinite(x) || x <= 0) return; if (x < 100) r.b++; else if (x < 300) r.m++; else r.p++; }); return r; }; let wm = []; try { wm = $('Reshape Walmart Response').first().json.walmartProducts || []; } catch (e) {} const w = band($('Reshape Wayfair Response').first().json.wayfair_products), a = band($('Reshape Amazon Response').first().json.amazonProducts), m = band(wm); return 'Budget (<$100): W: ' + w.b + ' | A: ' + a.b + ' | Wm: ' + m.b + '\nMid ($100-$300): W: ' + w.m + ' | A: ' + a.m + ' | Wm: ' + m.m + '\nPremium ($300+): W: ' + w.p + ' | A: ' + a.p + ' | Wm: ' + m.p; })()} PRECOMPUTED COUNTS BY PRICE RANGE (W = Wayfair | A = Amazon | Wm = Walmart; use these to judge where competitors are thin): ${(() => { const rs = [['$0-$50', 0, 50], ['$50-$100', 50, 100], ['$100-$200', 100, 200], ['$200-$400', 200, 400], ['$400+', 400, Infinity]]; const px = i => { const x = parseFloat(String(i.price ?? '').replace(/,/g, '')); return Number.isFinite(x) && x > 0 ? x : NaN; }; const cnt = (items, r) => (items || []).filter(i => { const x = px(i); return Number.isFinite(x) && x >= r[1] && x < r[2]; }).length; let wm = []; try { wm = $('Reshape Walmart Response').first().json.walmartProducts || []; } catch (e) {} const W = $('Reshape Wayfair Response').first().json.wayfair_products, A = $('Reshape Amazon Response').first().json.amazonProducts; return rs.map(r => r[0] + ': W: ' + cnt(W, r) + ' | A: ' + cnt(A, r) + ' | Wm: ' + cnt(wm, r)).join('\n'); })()} WAYFAIR PRODUCTS: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Wayfair Response').first().json.wayfair_products?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)} AMAZON COMPETITOR DATA: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Amazon Response').first().json.amazonProducts?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)} WALMART COMPETITOR DATA: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Walmart Response').first().json.walmartProducts?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)}` } ], stream: false }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-Q4_K_M.gguf", messages: [ { role: "system", content: `You are a senior strategy consultant. Based on all the analysis of Wayfair vs Amazon vs Walmart, provide actionable recommendations. TASK: Create Strategic Recommendations with clear prioritization and visual hierarchy. PROVIDE: 1. 2-3 Quick Wins (immediate actions, high impact) 2. 3-4 Strategic Initiatives (longer-term plays) 3. Each recommendation needs: title, description, priority level, expected impact 4. At least one recommendation should specifically address Walmart competition 5. At least one recommendation should specifically address Amazon competition OUTPUT FORMAT (HTML only, no markdown):

Strategic Recommendations

🚀 Quick Wins (Immediate Actions)

1. [Recommendation Title]

[Detailed description - 2-3 sentences explaining what to do and why. Mention which competitor this addresses (Amazon/Walmart/Both).]

High Priority Impact: High

2. [Recommendation Title]

[Detailed description addressing specific competitor threat or opportunity.]

High Priority Impact: High

📊 Strategic Initiatives

3. [Strategic Initiative Title]

[Longer description - explain the strategy, which competitor gap it exploits, and expected outcomes.]

High Priority Impact: High

4. [Strategic Initiative Title]

[Description of medium-priority initiative.]

Medium Priority Impact: Medium

5. [Strategic Initiative Title]

[Description - could be about differentiation, new product lines, or market positioning.]

Medium Priority Impact: Medium

6. [Lower Priority Initiative]

[Description of a nice-to-have or longer-term exploration.]

Low Priority Impact: Medium
PRIORITY GUIDELINES: - priority-high: Urgent, addresses immediate competitive threat, high ROI - priority-medium: Important but not urgent, builds long-term advantage - priority-low: Nice to have, exploratory, or requires more research CONTENT GUIDELINES: - Be specific - reference actual findings from the analysis - Mention specific competitors by name (Amazon, Walmart) - Reference specific price points or product gaps identified - Include actionable next steps, not vague suggestions - Each recommendation should tie back to data from earlier sections EXAMPLES OF GOOD RECOMMENDATIONS: - "Launch a $80-$150 'Value Plus' line to compete with Walmart's large-format rugs" - "Expand machine-washable selection to counter Amazon's Soalmost success" - "Create 'Designer Picks' collections to differentiate from Amazon's Ophanie dominance"` }, { role: "user", content: `CATEGORY: ${$('Input Parser').first().json.categoryDisplayName} EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: ${JSON.stringify($('Executive Summary Generator').first().json.choices[0].message.content)} AMAZON ANALYSIS: ${JSON.stringify($('Amazon Analysis Generator').first().json.choices[0].message.content)} COMPARISON: ${JSON.stringify($('Comparison Generator').first().json.choices[0].message.content)} PRICING & WHITESPACE: ${JSON.stringify($('Pricing & Whitespace Generator').first().json.choices[0].message.content)}` } ], stream: false }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-Q4_K_M.gguf", messages: [ { role: "system", content: `You are a sourcing analyst specializing in home goods supply chain. Identify suppliers and brands from competitor product data. TASK: Create a Supplier Identification & Sourcing Opportunities section. ANALYZE THE DATA TO: 1. Extract all unique brand/supplier names from Amazon and Walmart products 2. Identify which brands are NOT currently on Wayfair 3. Note what each supplier is known for (style, price point, features) 4. Find sourcing opportunities for Wayfair OUTPUT FORMAT (HTML only, no markdown):

Supplier Identification & Sourcing Opportunities

Major Suppliers / Brands Observed

Supplier / Brand Platform Known For Price Range Website
[Brand Name] [Amazon/Walmart/Both] [Brief description - style, features, target market] $[X] - $[Y] [Website or "Amazon Storefront"]

Sourcing Opportunities

🎯 Brands Not Currently on Wayfair

The following suppliers are active on Amazon/Walmart but appear absent from Wayfair's catalog:

  • [Brand] - [Why they'd be valuable: style, price point, reviews]
  • [Brand] - [Why they'd be valuable]
  • [Brand] - [Why they'd be valuable]
High Priority

⚡ Style Gaps to Fill

These suppliers offer styles or products that could fill gaps in Wayfair's assortment:

  • [Brand] specializes in [style] which Wayfair lacks depth in
  • [Brand] offers [feature/style] at competitive price points
Medium Priority

🏭 Private Label / Exclusive Candidates

These suppliers may be suitable for private label partnerships or exclusive arrangements:

  • [Brand] - [Why: quality, price point, style alignment]
  • [Brand] - [Why: manufacturing capability, unique features]
Medium Priority

Key Supplier Insights

  • Amazon Dominance: [Which brand dominates Amazon in this category and why]
  • Walmart Focus: [What type of suppliers Walmart features]
  • Price Point Gaps: [Where supplier opportunities exist by price]
  • Emerging Brands: [Any newer brands showing strong reviews/traction]
BRAND IDENTIFICATION TIPS: - Look for brand names in product titles (usually first word or after "by") - Common Amazon rug brands: Ophanie, Rugs.com, Safavieh, nuLOOM, Unique Loom, Gorilla Grip, Lahome - Common Walmart rug brands: Mainstays, Better Homes & Gardens, SAFAVIEH, Pentantan, My Texas House - If brand website unknown, link to their Amazon/Walmart storefront or write "Search Required" IMPORTANT: - Only include brands you can actually identify from the product data - Compare against Wayfair's manufacturer list to identify gaps - Be realistic about private label candidates (smaller brands, quality products) - Include at least 5 brands in the main table` }, { role: "user", content: `CATEGORY: ${$('Input Parser').first().json.categoryDisplayName} AMAZON ANALYSIS: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Amazon Response').first().json.amazonProducts?.map(p => ({ name: p.name, brand: p.brand, url: p.url, price: p.price })).slice(0, 15), null, 2)} EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: ${JSON.stringify($('Executive Summary Generator').first().json.choices[0].message.content)} WALMART PRODUCTS: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Walmart Response').first().json.walmartProducts?.map(p => ({ name: p.name, brand: p.brand, url: p.url, price: p.price })).slice(0, 15), null, 2)} WAYFAIR PRODUCTS: ${JSON.stringify($('Reshape Wayfair Response').first().json.wayfair_products?.map(p => ({ title: p.title, manufacturer: p.manufacturer })).slice(0, 15), null, 2) }` } ], stream: false }) }}
